title: super-board skill map

kinds.public: skill or command a user triggers directly
kinds.lane: board lane skill: started by /super-board run, also runnable standalone
kinds.external: skill from outside the pack (origin field says where)
kinds.script: shell, python, node script or saved Workflow
kinds.board: state: GitHub Project, config, ledgers, repo

nodes.label: /super-board
nodes.what: The autonomous GitHub-Project pipeline: five verbs (onboard, lint, status, run, stop) take one board shape (Backlog · Ready · Building · QA · Review · Blocked · Done) from empty to drained, with labels qa · bug · feature routing each card.
nodes.when: Eric types /super-board <verb>, or says "drain my GitHub project" or "stop super-board"; with no verb it asks which one.
nodes.how: The session is an orchestrator only: it routes the verb to its reference file, dispatches lane agents, and never does product work itself. Board state is the only state, so `run` is also resume. Every commit, ticket, PR body and comment follows references/writing-standard.md.
nodes.author: EricTechPro

nodes.label: /super-collect
nodes.what: Finds problems in one project and files them as verified tickets into its super-board Backlog: five built-in sources plus any custom source added in onboard. It never builds, edits app code, or moves a card to Ready.
nodes.when: Eric runs /super-collect (all enabled sources) or /super-collect <source…> with sentry, posthog, github, prs, architecture or a custom source's name; optional --since and --yes.
nodes.how: Fetches each source for the window (default 14 days), sends every candidate to one fresh verifier sub-agent, then files through super-collect-file.sh. Dry-run by default: it shows a plan table and files on confirm.
nodes.sublabel: sentry · posthog · github · prs · architecture · custom
nodes.author: EricTechPro

nodes.label: /ui-refine-loop
nodes.what: Unattended Impeccable check-then-fix loop on one page or component that ends in a draft PR with a Before | After table. Standalone: no board lane ever starts it.
nodes.when: Eric runs /ui-refine-loop <route | component | description> ["what's wrong"] [--rounds N], or says "refine loop" or "polish this page with impeccable".
nodes.how: Reads the target's code, grills Eric (at most 10 questions) into a taste file, then runs the saved ui-refine-loop workflow: each round fresh checkers rank typed problems and a fresh fixer chains Impeccable verbs, polish last. Default 5 rounds; a finish reviewer grades every fix. Commits are `💄 [ui] <slug>: …` and the PR body uses super-board-pr-body.sh's marker blocks.
nodes.author: EricTechPro

nodes.label: /visual
nodes.what: Turns the current work into one self-contained HTML page: a branch recap, a plan, or a map of a folder or architecture, with diagrams, a file map and annotated code.
nodes.when: Eric runs /visual, /visual recap [base], /visual plan [file] or /visual <path>; with no argument visual.py detect picks the mode.
nodes.how: Writes a data.json from git facts or the plan, then visual.py render injects it into an inline template with no build step. It screenshots the page headless to check it, and offers to publish only on a yes.
nodes.author: EricTechPro

nodes.label: /super-board onboard
nodes.what: An 8-step setup wizard (Checks · GitHub · Board · Branch · AGENTS.md · Policies · Bug sources · Review) that installs or repairs what the board needs and writes the config once.
nodes.when: Eric runs /super-board onboard (or /super-board:super-board onboard after a plugin install), on a new project, after an upgrade from 2.x, or to check and repair an existing setup.
nodes.how: One AskUserQuestion per step with the recommended option first; must-haves are fixed without asking by super-board-setup.py. Answers save to onboard-answers.json as they come, so a halt resumes, and repo files change only at step 8 after "Write everything". It ends by naming /super-board lint.
nodes.author: EricTechPro

nodes.label: /super-board lint
nodes.what: Pre-flight readiness check that walks Ready, Building, QA and Review, flags issues that fail any of 18 criteria, proposes a qa/bug/feature label, and dispatches a helper skill per flagged issue.
nodes.when: Eric runs /super-board lint before a run, typically after /super-collect filed new Backlog cards.
nodes.how: Criteria 13–18 cover what the loop needs: a parseable `## Blocked by` line, a fake with no follow-up card, too big (over ~400 changed lines or many areas), the ticket sections, a checklist AC, and lettered Context steps. Phase 4 routes each flagged pattern to one skill sub-agent while Eric keeps the pace.
nodes.author: EricTechPro

nodes.label: /super-board status
nodes.what: Read-only snapshot of the active config, every column in board order (Backlog included), and in-flight workers.
nodes.when: Eric runs /super-board status to see where a run stands.
nodes.how: super-board-status.py reads the board and local in-flight state and prints the columns in the board's own order; it changes nothing.
nodes.author: EricTechPro

nodes.label: /super-board run
nodes.what: The autonomous loop: repeated waves of the super-board-wave workflow from this session until the board drains or a halt gate fires. Also the resume command.
nodes.when: Eric runs /super-board run [--low|--high] [<slug>]; the default worker_backend "workflow" stays in-session, "claude-p" opts into the legacy headless runner.
nodes.how: Each wave: rate and usage guard, plan with super-board-wave-plan.sh (which refuses an old `variant: qa-only` config with exit 65), act on sweep/flag/stranded/resume, claim cards by assignee, launch the workflow, reconcile, report. Halts after 3 zero-progress waves, a high block rate, or a stop.
nodes.author: EricTechPro

nodes.label: /super-board stop
nodes.what: Graceful shutdown: stops the wave, posts "stopped mid-flight" comments, releases assignee claims, and removes the wave lock so the next run resumes.
nodes.when: Eric runs /super-board stop or says "stop the run" / "pause the loop".
nodes.how: Stops the workflow (or kills the legacy dispatcher via super-board-stop.sh), comments on every in-flight issue and PR, and strips bot_identity assignees. Resume is just `run` again.
nodes.author: EricTechPro

nodes.label: super-build
nodes.what: Builder lane: takes a pre-flighted Ready card into its own worktree, makes the smallest safe change test-first under the 400-line PR cap, opens a draft PR and moves the card to QA. It never merges.
nodes.when: Started by the board: the super-board-wave workflow runs it for Ready cards labelled feature or bug (or unlabelled) once pre-flight says proceed. Also runnable standalone as /super-build (legacy headless claude -p dispatch).
nodes.how: Follows run.md's Builder lifecycle. An explicit `Skills:` line wins, else the type label picks the chain, always plus ponytail first, verification-before-completion and a code-review of its own diff. Past the size cap mid-build it stops and proposes a /to-tickets split. Commits and PR blocks follow the writing standard via super-board-pr-body.sh.
nodes.author: EricTechPro

nodes.label: super-qa
nodes.what: Tester lane: builds an issue-scoped test plan, runs a test-gap check on the Builder's diff, captures evidence and screenshots, then passes the card to Review or bounces it to Build.
nodes.when: Started by the board for cards in QA, and straight from Ready for cards labelled qa (they skip Building). Also runnable standalone as /super-qa, a BFS route-crawling bug-bash, or /super-qa <url> for a live site with no repo.
nodes.how: One observable test per AC plus the test-gap ledger, High gaps written red-first. On a qa card it creates the issue branch itself and files real defects as bug cards. It ticks the PR's ac block, writes visual and history rows with super-board-pr-body.sh, and posts `[qa] [report]` comments with screenshots pinned to a sha.
nodes.author: EricTechPro

nodes.label: super-review
nodes.what: Reviewer lane and standalone PR review: forms its own hypotheses first, remembers prior findings, classes every finding, and merges only through the merge gate.
nodes.when: Started by the board for cards in Review (always on the session model). Also runnable standalone when Eric says "review this branch" or "is this merge-ready".
nodes.how: Thread scan, prior-report round 1, own pass with code-review, codebase-design and ponytail-review, a rerun of the Tester's exact test command, then an adversarial truth-check on non-trivial diffs. One report comment is edited in place every round. A clean review merges through the gate pinned to the reviewed head SHA; exit 7 or 8 parks the card in Blocked with 🙋. Visual problems become a UI ticket, never a ui-refine-loop run. The truth-check sub-agents get a fixed verbatim brief, and Over-engineering is never a Blocker from any of them.
nodes.author: EricTechPro

nodes.label: GitHub Project board
nodes.what: The configured GitHub Project with seven columns (Backlog, Ready, Building, QA, Review, Blocked, Done) and three routing labels (qa, bug, feature); the only loop state. There is no Skipped column.
nodes.when: Read and written on every wave, by every lane move, and by /super-collect filing into Backlog.
nodes.how: Cards move by `gh project item-edit`; assignees act as claim mutexes; PR threads start with their owner lane [builder] / [qa] / [reviewer] plus a label. A card dropped on purpose is closed as not planned and moved to Done with a 🤷 comment.

nodes.label: super-board config
nodes.what: Per-project JSON config: board, base branch, timezone, the seven columns, labels, merge_policy, migrations, worker backend, model tier, truth gate, plus `collect` (sources and custom[]) and `refine` blocks. No `variant` key.
nodes.when: Written once by onboard at step 8 (and migrated to v3 keys by super-board-setup.py fix); read at the start of every run, collect and ui-refine-loop setup.
nodes.how: Lives at `.claude/super-board/configs/<slug>.json` with `.claude/super-board/active` pointing at it, validated against config-schema.json.

nodes.label: repo · base branch
nodes.what: The project's git repo and configured base branch (never assumed to be main); a card is Done only when its merge commit is an ancestor of it.
nodes.when: Changed only by a merge-gate squash-merge; read by /visual and branched from by every worktree.
nodes.how: Lanes and ui-refine-loop work on their own branches under .worktrees/ or .claude/worktrees/; the opt-in protected-push guard can block direct pushes to it.

nodes.label: run manifest
nodes.what: Per-run ledger at `docs/super-board/runs/<date>-<slug>.md`, one line per card per wave.
nodes.when: Appended during each wave's reconcile step.
nodes.how: Each line records card, lanes run, final status, column and detail: `| #N | <lanesRun> | <finalStatus> | <column> | <detail> |`.

nodes.label: Super Ultimate QA board
nodes.what: Separate GitHub Project (Queue, Testing, Done, Bug, Flaky, Skip) used by standalone /super-qa as its loop state.
nodes.when: Written when a standalone super-qa iteration finds a red spec; /super-collect bugs and qa-card defects also go through the same filer.
nodes.how: super-qa-file-bug.sh creates a `source:qa` issue with the evidence body and sets its Status to Bug (Flaky and Skip for the other outcomes).

nodes.label: taste + direction file
nodes.what: Per-project design taste file (default `docs/design/taste.md`) holding the grill's goal, direction, keep and avoid answers plus taste rules and slop tells.
nodes.when: Written after the grill and committed as the refine branch's first commit; read first by every checker, fixer and finish reviewer.
nodes.how: Starts from the neutral references/taste.md when absent; each target gets a `### <target>` block under Direction, with "you pick" answers marked (picked).

nodes.label: refine ledger
nodes.what: The only memory carried between refine rounds: one line per check with score /40, before-vs-now, and problem ids.
nodes.when: Appended by the workflow after every check; written to `<run>/ledger.md` at finish.
nodes.how: Checkers reuse ledger ids so a problem that survives three checks is called out; stop rules read it (two clean checks, two reverts in a row).

nodes.label: refine draft PR
nodes.what: The draft PR from `refine/<slug>` against the recorded base branch, with a Before | After table, score line and finish grades.
nodes.when: Opened once at the end of a ui-refine-loop run; never merged by the loop.
nodes.how: pr-shots.sh commits round-0 and final shots to `docs/ui-refine/<slug>/` and prints a Before | After table pinned to both shas; the body uses the writing standard's marker blocks (status, problem, solution, ac, history, visual, risk) and is humanized before `gh pr create --draft`.

nodes.label: open GitHub issues
nodes.what: The repo's open issues that are not yet on the board and carry no `source:*` label.
nodes.when: Read by the /super-collect github source.
nodes.how: Fetched with `gh issue list --state open`; real work is adopted onto the board (`--adopt <n>`), never copied into a new issue.

nodes.label: .claude/settings.json
nodes.what: The target project's Claude Code settings, where install.sh merges the guard hook block from settings-snippet.json.
nodes.when: Written by install.sh (backed up first, never adding a command twice); read by Claude Code at every session.
nodes.how: Wires PreToolUse, PostToolUse and SessionStart commands to the scripts copied into `.claude/hooks/`; `--protect-main` adds settings-protect-main.json.

nodes.label: guard hooks
nodes.what: The pack's Claude Code hooks: four default guards, an opt-in push guard, post-merge worktree cleanup, and two dev-only hooks for the pack itself.
nodes.when: Installed by install.sh unless --no-hooks; each fires on its Claude Code event and matcher.
nodes.how: Python 3 stdlib scripts that read hook JSON on stdin, print a decision only when they block, and exit 0 on their own errors so a broken guard never stops work.

nodes.label: guard-worktree-path
nodes.what: Denies `git worktree add|move` whose target resolves outside `<repo>/.claude/worktrees/`.
nodes.when: PreToolUse, matcher Bash, on every shell command.
nodes.how: Parses the command, honouring `cd X &&` and `git -C X`, resolves the target path, and blocks when it escapes the worktrees folder.

nodes.label: guard-secrets
nodes.what: Denies reading or piping dotenv files, SSH keys, .npmrc, credentials(.json), service-account JSON and .pem files; .env.example stays readable.
nodes.when: PreToolUse, matcher Bash|Read|Grep.
nodes.how: Matches file paths in Read/Grep input and in shell commands against secret-file patterns and blocks the call. One plain call to super-board-env-check.sh (no pipe, chain or redirect) is allowed, since it prints only present / empty / missing.

nodes.label: guard-key-literals
nodes.what: Stops a live-looking API key from being written into a file, and flags one already on disk.
nodes.when: PreToolUse on Edit|MultiEdit|Write|NotebookEdit|Bash, and PostToolUse on Edit|MultiEdit|Write|NotebookEdit.
nodes.how: Scans the content being written for key-shaped literals and reports line numbers only, never the value.

nodes.label: guard-delete-outside
nodes.what: Denies rm, rmdir, unlink, find -delete / -exec rm and git clean whose target resolves outside $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR, and always `/` or `~` itself.
nodes.when: PreToolUse, matcher Bash.
nodes.how: Resolves each target (honouring cd, git -C, ~ and $HOME); temp dirs stay allowed, and a path known only at run time is allowed.

nodes.label: guard-protected-push
nodes.what: Opt-in guard that denies a git push that would update or delete main, master, any configured base_branch, or a name in SB_PROTECTED_BRANCHES.
nodes.when: PreToolUse, matcher Bash, only after onboard's Policies yes (step 6) or `./install.sh --protect-main`.
nodes.how: Catches force pushes, explicit refspecs, --delete, --all/--mirror and a bare push while the base is checked out; feature-branch force pushes stay allowed. SB_ALLOW_PROTECTED_PUSH=1 turns it off for a session.

nodes.label: cleanup-wt
nodes.what: Removes worktrees and local branches already merged into a base branch; never deletes unmerged work.
nodes.when: SessionStart with `--auto --fetch` when a base tip moved since the last session, and after every merge when the merge gate calls it with `--post-merge`.
nodes.how: Wip-commits a dirty worktree on a merged branch and keeps its branch, never touches bases or its own worktree, and writes a recovery TSV under `<git-common-dir>/cleanup-wt/` before acting.

nodes.label: gate-skill-evals (dev)
nodes.what: Dev-only Stop hook that blocks ending a session when a skill changed and no `claude plugin eval` result is newer than the change.
nodes.when: Stop event in the pack's own `.claude/settings.json` (and EricOS if added by hand); never installed into target projects.
nodes.how: A changed SKILL.md always counts; a changed reference, script or workflow counts when the skill has an eval case. SKILL_EVAL_GATE=off, a running eval or `.claude/eval-gate-ignore` globs stand it down.

nodes.label: readme-sync (dev)
nodes.what: Dev-only hooks that keep README.md's skill tables in step with skills/*/SKILL.md and families.json.
nodes.when: PostToolUse on Edit|Write|MultiEdit in the pack repo, and as a git pre-commit hook when it is symlinked in.
nodes.how: Runs super-board-readme-sync.py; the pre-commit version stops the commit when README.md had to change so it can be staged.

nodes.label: super-board-wave-plan.sh
nodes.what: Read-only planner that computes the next wave from board state: cards (each with its lane and labels) plus the sweep, flag, stranded and resume lists.
nodes.when: Run by the orchestrator at the start of every wave, after the rate and usage guards pass.
nodes.how: Reads the board and `## Blocked by` dependencies (via super-board-deps.sh); a Ready card labelled qa gets lane qa, every other Ready card lane build. `resume` lists 🙋 cards a human approved with `done`. A `variant: qa-only` config is refused with exit 65.

nodes.label: super-board-wave.js
nodes.what: Saved Workflow that drains one wave: a Pre-flight phase for cards about to be built, a haiku classify router, then Build, QA and Review lane agents per card.
nodes.when: Launched by /super-board run with {configPath, cards (with lane and labels), humanApprovesMerge, tier}; a stale `variant` other than full is refused.
nodes.how: Pre-flights Ready build cards in batches of 5 and never builds a card without a proceed verdict. The classifier keeps a card's qa/bug/feature label and adds feature or bug to unlabelled ones, never qa. A qa card goes Ready → QA. Model ladder by tier and complexity; Review always on the session model.

nodes.label: super-board-merge-gate.sh
nodes.what: The only path to the base branch: takes an atomic mkdir lock, applies merge_policy, re-proves the branch against the current base inside the lock, runs allowed DB migrations, then squash-merges.
nodes.when: Called by the Reviewer once a review passes (and human_approves_merge is not set).
nodes.how: super-board-merge-policy.py decides who merges: money, auth, destructive schema or a diff over auto_max_lines (400 changed lines, lockfiles/generated/snapshots/migration SQL excluded) exits 7; a migration it may not run or a declared human step exits 8. Otherwise it merges with `--match-head-commit` (exit 6 when the head moved) and runs cleanup-wt --post-merge.

nodes.label: super-qa-file-bug.sh
nodes.what: Files one finding as a GitHub issue with a validated body onto the Super Ultimate QA board.
nodes.when: Called by standalone super-qa on a red spec, and by super-collect-file.sh for bug, feature and fix tickets.
nodes.how: Rejects bodies missing the ticket-format sections (Problem · Context · Fix · Acceptance Criteria · Risk, bugs with the folded Evidence table) or holding placeholders; adds type, source, priority and area labels and sets the project Status, falling back through Bug, Ready, Todo, Backlog, Triage.

nodes.label: review-file-refactor.sh
nodes.what: Files a deepening opportunity as a `refactor` card, deduped by fingerprint.
nodes.when: Called by super-review for shape findings that must not block a merge, and by super-collect-file.sh for architecture tickets.
nodes.how: A body with an `## Acceptance criteria` section goes straight to Ready; otherwise it lands in the holding column for lint. It appends `## Blocked by` when missing.

nodes.label: super-collect-file.sh
nodes.what: Single filing entry point for /super-collect that routes each verified ticket to the pack's filers.
nodes.when: Called once per candidate the verifier marked file or needs-triage (dry-run without --yes, real filing with it), or with --adopt <n>.
nodes.how: bug/feature/fix go to super-qa-file-bug.sh, refactor to super-review-file-refactor.sh, every body in the writing-standard ticket format. It enforces per-source fingerprints (custom `custom|<name>|<key>`), exact-fingerprint dedupe and the board's holding column.

nodes.label: sentry fetcher
nodes.what: The sentry source: lists unresolved Sentry issues in the window and pulls event and tag evidence.
nodes.when: Run when /super-collect includes sentry and the config has a sentry block.
nodes.how: `collect_sentry.py list --since <w>` calls the Sentry REST API with SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN from .env; `check <id>` answers still-happening for the verifier. One issue becomes one bug, fp `err|sentry|<id>`.

nodes.label: posthog fetcher
nodes.what: The posthog source: exceptions, configured failure events, rage and dead clicks, web vitals, surveys, plus tracking gaps.
nodes.when: Run when /super-collect includes posthog.
nodes.how: `collect_posthog.py list|events|funnel|check` runs HogQL queries with POSTHOG_PERSONAL_API_KEY; signal groups over the thresholds become bugs, and missing workflow events become `analytics` feature tickets.

nodes.label: prs fetcher
nodes.what: The prs source: merged PRs in the window with their comments, reviews, review threads and flagged super-review reports.
nodes.when: Run when /super-collect includes prs.
nodes.how: `collect_prs.py list` runs one paginated GraphQL search; Claude then clusters recurring root causes at a shared boundary into fix, refactor or feature tickets (fp `prs|<boundary>|<cause>`).

nodes.label: shoot.mjs
nodes.what: Playwright screenshot script for the refine loop: light and dark at 1440 and 390, section crops, and before | after sheets.
nodes.when: Run for round-0 shots at setup and for AFTER shots at the end of every fix round.
nodes.how: Writes `<label>-<state>-<desktop|mobile>-<light|dark>.png` grown to the scroll height; `--compare round-0` adds cmp sheets the next checker judges.

nodes.label: impeccable detect
nodes.what: Impeccable's mechanical anti-pattern detector, run over every scope path holding markup or styles.
nodes.when: Run by the isolated detector sub-agent in every check, alongside the audit.
nodes.how: Invoked as `scripts/impeccable detect --json` (v4.4+) or `node scripts/detect.mjs --json` (v4.0.x), as found by refine-setup.sh detect; exit 2 means findings, which are checked in source for false positives.

nodes.label: install.sh
nodes.what: Installs the pack into a target project: skills, .claude/bin scripts, workflows and the guard hooks, with grouped emoji output.
nodes.when: Run by get.sh, by super-board-setup.py fix during onboard, or by hand: `./install.sh [--no-hooks] [--protect-main] [target]`.
nodes.how: Copies hooks/*.py to `.claude/hooks/` (never hooks/dev/) and merges the hook block through super-board-settings.py; `--no-hooks --protect-main` installs only the push guard. It records an older install in `.claude/super-board/upgrade.json` and ends with one next step: /super-board onboard.

nodes.label: visual.py
nodes.what: The /visual helper: detect picks the mode, facts collects git data, render injects data.json into the inline template.
nodes.when: Run by /visual at every step: detect with no argument, facts in recap mode, render after data.json is written.
nodes.how: render prints `{out, missingHunks}`; grounded hunks come from git via `hunks[].file + contains`, and output lands in a gitignored `_tmp/<date>-visual/` or `.visual/`.

nodes.label: grilling
nodes.what: Interview pattern that walks a design tree in rounds: numbered questions, each with a recommended answer, until the frontier is empty.
nodes.when: Reached by /ui-refine-loop's grill step and by /super-board lint for vague or multi-reading tickets; forbidden inside unattended workers.
nodes.how: Asks the whole frontier per round and waits; facts come from sub-agents, decisions from the user. ui-refine-loop caps it at 10 questions in waves of 3, then 4.
nodes.author: mattpocock

nodes.label: tdd
nodes.what: Test-driven development discipline: tests at agreed seams through public interfaces, red before green, one vertical slice at a time.
nodes.when: Reached by super-build for every non-docs ticket, by super-qa when writing High test gaps, and by implement.
nodes.how: Defines good tests, the anti-patterns (implementation-coupled, tautological, horizontal slicing) and the loop rules; refactoring belongs to the code-review stage.
nodes.author: mattpocock

nodes.label: tdd-v2
nodes.what: The EricOS testing ladder: which rung a test belongs at (unit, isolated render, e2e) and the gate for climbing to the next.
nodes.when: Reached by super-qa's test-gap check "where the repo has it", and by implement as its preferred test skill.
nodes.how: Building climbs bottom-up; chasing a defect walks down to the first rung that still reproduces. It owns the layer and defers red-green discipline to tdd.
nodes.author: EricTechPro

nodes.label: implement
nodes.what: Implements a piece of work from a spec or tickets, test-first, then reviews and commits it.
nodes.when: Reached by super-build when the issue's type label is feature or ux (implement → tdd → codebase-design).
nodes.how: Uses tdd-v2 at pre-agreed seams with tdd underneath, runs typecheck and single tests often and the full suite once, then runs code-review before committing.
nodes.author: mattpocock

nodes.label: code-review
nodes.what: Two-axis review of the diff since a fixed point: Standards (repo rules plus a Fowler smell baseline) and Spec (does it match the issue).
nodes.when: Reached by super-build once against its own diff before the final commit, by super-review on every card, and by implement and tdd.
nodes.how: Pins the fixed point (the lanes pass the merge-base so it never asks), runs a Standards and a Spec sub-agent in parallel, and reports them side by side without reranking.
nodes.author: mattpocock

nodes.label: diagnosing-bugs
nodes.what: Diagnosis loop for hard bugs and perf regressions: build a tight red feedback loop, reproduce, hypothesise, instrument, fix with a regression test.
nodes.when: Reached by super-build for `bug`-labelled tickets, by super-qa as a required dependency, and by lint for bug tickets with no repro.
nodes.how: Six phases; refuses to theorise before one command goes red on this bug. Its post-mortem hands off to improve-codebase-architecture when no good seam exists.
nodes.author: mattpocock

nodes.label: codebase-design
nodes.what: Shared deep-module vocabulary: module, interface, depth, seam, adapter, leverage, locality, and the deletion test.
nodes.when: Reached by super-build for feature and refactor tickets, by super-review in step 2 and for every deepening opportunity, and by super-collect's architecture finder as a fallback.
nodes.how: A reference to consult, not a session: no report, no prompts. Its design-it-twice pattern runs parallel sub-agents when an interface needs alternatives.
nodes.author: mattpocock

nodes.label: ask-matt
nodes.what: Router over the Matt Pocock skills: which flow fits the situation, from idea to ship.
nodes.when: Reached by super-build and super-qa workers when the right flow is unclear.
nodes.how: Main flow: grill-with-docs, optional prototype via handoff, to-spec and to-tickets for multi-session work, then implement (driving tdd) and code-review. On-ramps: triage, diagnosing-bugs, wayfinder.
nodes.author: mattpocock

nodes.label: humanizer
nodes.what: Strips AI writing tells from a finished draft so it reads like a person wrote it, with Eric Tech plain-words overrides.
nodes.when: Reached whenever a lane or ui-refine-loop writes prose: the writing standard says ALWAYS run commits, tickets, PR bodies and comments through it when installed.
nodes.how: Applies the vendored blader/humanizer rule set (32 patterns) as a silent pass; without it the writing standard's plain-words rules apply (short sentences, plain words, no hype).
nodes.author: blader

nodes.label: verification-before-compl.
nodes.what: Evidence before assertions: run the verification command and read its output before claiming work is done, fixed or passing.
nodes.when: Reached by super-build before its final commit and by super-qa as a required dependency.
nodes.how: A gate function: identify the proving command, run it fresh, read the full output, and only then state the result.
nodes.author: obra

nodes.label: context7 (docs)
nodes.what: MCP docs lookup used to read current official documentation for a library or API version.
nodes.when: Reached by super-build when a ticket touches a third-party API, an upgrade, or auth/billing.
nodes.how: Builder reads the exact surface and installed major's docs (context7 when available, else vendor docs by web search) and cites them as `Docs:` bullets in the PR's Solution block.
nodes.author: upstash

nodes.label: resolving-merge-conflicts
nodes.what: Resolves an in-progress merge or rebase conflict by reading each side's intent, then runs the project's checks.
nodes.when: Reached by super-build on a live conflict, e.g. when the merge gate exits 2 or 5 and the card returns to the Builder, and by /git-sync when its pull conflicts.
nodes.how: Finds primary sources per hunk, preserves both intents where possible, never aborts; the Builder's finish line is green verification, not an empty conflict list.
nodes.author: mattpocock

nodes.label: improve-codebase-arch.
nodes.what: Scans a codebase for deepening opportunities, presents them as an HTML report, then grills through the one picked.
nodes.when: Reached by /super-collect's architecture finder (findings only, no report or grilling) and by diagnosing-bugs' post-mortem; never loaded inside the Review lane.
nodes.how: Explores hot spots from git history with codebase-design vocabulary and CONTEXT.md/ADRs, writes the report, then runs grilling and domain-modeling on the chosen candidate.
nodes.author: mattpocock

nodes.label: domain-modeling
nodes.what: Sharpens a project's domain language in CONTEXT.md and records hard-to-reverse decisions as ADRs.
nodes.when: Reached from improve-codebase-architecture, grill-with-docs, triage and wayfinder sessions, and listed in super-build's skill map for terminology and ADRs.
nodes.how: Challenges fuzzy or overloaded terms and updates CONTEXT.md inline; offers an ADR only when a future reader would need the reason.
nodes.author: mattpocock

nodes.label: ponytail
nodes.what: Forces the simplest solution that works via a ladder: needed at all, already in the codebase, stdlib, native, installed dep, one line, then minimal code.
nodes.when: Reached by super-build on every ticket, before the first line of code (full intensity).
nodes.how: Runs after understanding the problem; bug fixes go to the root cause in the shared function. Inline ladder fallback when the plugin is absent.
nodes.author: DietrichGebert

nodes.label: ponytail-review
nodes.what: Diff review that hunts only over-engineering, one line per finding tagged delete, stdlib, native, yagni or shrink.
nodes.when: Reached by super-review on the merge-base diff in step 3.
nodes.how: Ends with `net: -N lines possible`; findings are Over-engineering, always Should fix and never a merge blocker alone. It applies nothing.
nodes.author: DietrichGebert

nodes.label: ponytail-audit
nodes.what: Whole-repo version of ponytail-review: a ranked list of what to delete, simplify or replace with stdlib or native features.
nodes.when: Reached by /super-collect's architecture finder for over-engineering findings.
nodes.how: Same tags as ponytail-review, biggest cut first, ending `net: -N lines, -M deps possible`; one-shot and read-only.
nodes.author: DietrichGebert

nodes.label: impeccable
nodes.what: Frontend design skill whose commands critique, audit and refine UI: build, evaluate, refine, enhance, fix and iterate categories.
nodes.when: Reached by /ui-refine-loop at setup (detect and context), by every checker and fixer, and by lint for shape and clarify.
nodes.how: Each command has a playbook under reference/<command>.md plus craft-floor.md; refine-setup.sh finds v4.0.x node scripts or the v4.4+ launcher in this or any parent dir, warning loudly when missing.
nodes.author: pbakaus

nodes.label: testing-strategy
nodes.what: Coverage judgment per component type: what is worth testing and what to skip.
nodes.when: Listed by super-build's skill map and super-qa's dependencies for deciding which kind of test a change needs.
nodes.how: Informs coverage only; the localisation ladder, not this skill, picks the test layer. Not installed in EricOS.

nodes.label: vitest
nodes.what: Mechanics for unit and integration tests in a TS/JS repo.
nodes.when: Listed by super-qa and super-build when the localisation ladder stops at unit or integration in a TS/JS repo.
nodes.how: Its references (core-expect, features-mocking, features-coverage, core-hooks, advanced-vi) guide test code. Not installed in EricOS.

nodes.label: playwright-best-practices
nodes.what: Mechanics for browser e2e specs: locators, fixtures, test data factories, page objects.
nodes.when: Listed by super-qa when writing or refactoring a Playwright spec.
nodes.how: data-testid first with getByRole fallback, custom fixtures for auth and seeding, POM for reusable interactions. Not installed in EricOS.

nodes.label: qa-test-planner
nodes.what: Test-plan helper lint dispatches for QA tickets with a vague test surface.
nodes.when: Reached by /super-board lint Phase 4 for QA tickets whose test surface is vague.
nodes.how: One sub-agent per flagged issue drafts a concrete test plan. Not installed in EricOS.

nodes.label: setup-matt-pocock-skills
nodes.what: One-time repo setup for the engineering skills: issue tracker, triage label vocabulary, domain doc layout.
nodes.when: Reached when code-review, to-spec, to-tickets, triage or wayfinder find `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md` missing.
nodes.how: Asks a few sections with recommended answers and records them under docs/agents/ so the other skills know whether to call gh or write markdown files.
nodes.author: mattpocock

nodes.label: grill-with-docs
nodes.what: Stateful grilling that builds CONTEXT.md and ADRs and checkpoints every answer to a capture file.
nodes.when: Reached from ask-matt as step 1 of the main flow whenever there is a working directory.
nodes.how: Runs the grilling primitive and drives domain-modeling to keep the glossary clean; user-invoked only.
nodes.author: EricTechPro

nodes.label: prototype
nodes.what: Throwaway prototype that answers one design question: a logic demo or a UI to look at.
nodes.when: Reached from ask-matt when a question needs a runnable answer, and from wayfinder prototype tickets.
nodes.how: Throwaway from day one, trivial to run, no persistence, no polish; the learning is handed back via handoff.
nodes.author: mattpocock

nodes.label: handoff
nodes.what: Compacts the conversation into a handoff document for a fresh agent.
nodes.when: Reached from ask-matt to bridge a prototype detour or a phase boundary.
nodes.how: Writes the summary to the OS temp directory, not the workspace, so another session can pick it up.
nodes.author: mattpocock

nodes.label: to-spec
nodes.what: Turns the current conversation into a spec and publishes it to the issue tracker, no interview.
nodes.when: Reached from ask-matt for multi-session builds; listed in super-build's skill map.
nodes.how: Writes the spec from a template and applies the `ready-for-agent` label; needs the tracker config from setup-matt-pocock-skills.
nodes.author: mattpocock

nodes.label: to-tickets
nodes.what: Breaks a plan or spec into tracer-bullet tickets, each declaring its blocking edges.
nodes.when: Reached from ask-matt after to-spec, and from /super-board lint to split a too-big ticket (criterion 15) into vertical slices; its `## Blocked by` template is why lint criterion 13 exists.
nodes.how: Publishes blockers first so edges reference real ids, as files locally or native blocking links on a real tracker.
nodes.author: mattpocock

nodes.label: triage
nodes.what: Moves raw issues and external PRs through a state machine of triage roles into agent-ready briefs.
nodes.when: Reached from ask-matt when bugs and requests pile up that you did not create.
nodes.how: Categorise, verify, grill if needed, write the brief; every comment carries an AI disclaimer and labels come from setup-matt-pocock-skills.
nodes.author: mattpocock

nodes.label: wayfinder
nodes.what: Charts a shared map of decision tickets for a huge, foggy effort and resolves them one at a time.
nodes.when: Reached from ask-matt for greenfield projects or builds too big for one session.
nodes.how: Tickets are research, prototype, grilling or task, HITL or AFK; it hands off to to-spec when the map clears instead of building.
nodes.author: mattpocock

nodes.label: impeccable fix verbs
nodes.what: The 15 Impeccable commands the ui-refine-loop fixer may chain, one per problem type, with polish always last.
nodes.when: Each fix round, after the checker returns ranked, typed P0–P3 problems.
nodes.how: The workflow attaches routing.md's default command per type and suggests a chain (severity order, structural before surface, additive verbs only when the direction asks); the fixer reads each playbook and craft-floor, then makes the final call.
nodes.author: pbakaus

nodes.label: motion + perf verbs
nodes.what: The last tier of the chain before polish: animate, delight and optimize.
nodes.when: When a problem is typed needs-motion, personality or performance.
nodes.how: routing.md runs these after the structural, surface and fix tiers; animate and delight are additive, so they run only when the brief or taste direction asks for more.
nodes.author: pbakaus

nodes.label: critique
nodes.what: UX design review with scoring; the loop uses Assessment A only, scored /20 across specificity, hierarchy, typography, color and composition.
nodes.when: Every check, run by the isolated design reviewer sub-agent in parallel with the detector.
nodes.how: Reads critique.md (Assessment A) and craft-floor.md, every shot and crop in both themes and widths, then the scope files; returns up to 8 typed problems. No Nielsen heuristics.
nodes.author: pbakaus

nodes.label: audit
nodes.what: Technical quality check scored /20 across accessibility, performance, responsive, theming and implementation integrity.
nodes.when: Every check, run by the isolated detector sub-agent after impeccable detect.
nodes.how: Reads audit.md, scores five dimensions 0–4, and turns each verified detector cluster or audit gap into a typed problem; it never sees the screenshots or the design review.
nodes.author: pbakaus

nodes.label: polish
nodes.what: Final quality pass over everything the round touched: small misalignments and inconsistencies, no structural change.
nodes.when: Always the last command of every fix round, even when no problem was typed polish.
nodes.how: Runs once over all touched files after the routed chain; then checks must be green before the round's single commit.
nodes.author: pbakaus

nodes.label: distill
nodes.what: Strips a surface to its essence, removing duplicate actions and competing chrome.
nodes.when: Routed for problems typed `cluttered`.
nodes.how: Structural tier, so it runs first in the chain alongside extract; follows reference/distill.md as a refinement of the existing design.
nodes.author: pbakaus

nodes.label: bolder
nodes.what: Amplifies a safe, bland design so it has more presence.
nodes.when: Routed for `bland`, only when the brief or taste direction asks for more.
nodes.how: Additive surface-tier verb; skipped with a reason like "direction says calmer", and dropped when it pulls against quieter on the same element.
nodes.author: pbakaus

nodes.label: quieter
nodes.what: Tones down an aggressive design: fewer colors, weights, borders, shadows or badges.
nodes.when: Routed for problems typed `too-loud`.
nodes.how: Surface tier after layout/adapt; when it conflicts with bolder on one element the higher-severity problem wins.
nodes.author: pbakaus

nodes.label: colorize
nodes.what: Adds strategic color where gray or flat UI should carry meaning.
nodes.when: Routed for `dull-color`, only when the direction asks for more.
nodes.how: Additive surface-tier verb; changes must hold in light and dark and use tokens, not raw values.
nodes.author: pbakaus

nodes.label: layout
nodes.what: Fixes spacing, rhythm, grouping, alignment and visual hierarchy.
nodes.when: Routed for problems typed `spacing-hierarchy`.
nodes.how: Second tier, after distill/extract; a cramped look caused by a copied card is rerouted to extract by the fixer.
nodes.author: pbakaus

nodes.label: typeset
nodes.what: Improves typography: fonts, type scale, weights, line length and figures.
nodes.when: Routed for problems typed `typography`.
nodes.how: Surface tier with colorize, quieter and bolder; follows reference/typeset.md within the taste file's type rules.
nodes.author: pbakaus

nodes.label: adapt
nodes.what: Adapts the surface to other screen sizes: breakpoints, touch targets, no sideways scroll at 390.
nodes.when: Routed for problems typed `responsive`.
nodes.how: Second tier with layout; the after shots at 390 in both themes prove it.
nodes.author: pbakaus

nodes.label: optimize
nodes.what: Diagnoses and fixes UI performance: jank, layout shift, heavy images or bundles.
nodes.when: Routed for problems typed `performance`.
nodes.how: Last tier with animate and delight, before polish; follows reference/optimize.md.
nodes.author: pbakaus

nodes.label: onboard
nodes.what: Designs first-run flows and empty states that point to the next action.
nodes.when: Routed for problems typed `first-run-empty`.
nodes.how: Fix tier with clarify and harden; no dense fixture means no dense shots, never fabricated data.
nodes.author: pbakaus

nodes.label: clarify
nodes.what: Improves UX copy: labels, errors, status words and instructions.
nodes.when: Routed for `confusing-copy` in the refine loop; also dispatched by /super-board lint for copy or error-message ACs.
nodes.how: Fix tier; refinement keeps the meaning of factual copy and never adds claims.
nodes.author: pbakaus

nodes.label: harden
nodes.what: Production-readiness: long content, errors, loading, i18n, overflow, and accessibility (contrast, focus, names, keyboard).
nodes.when: Routed for problems typed `edge-cases` or `accessibility`.
nodes.how: Fix tier; the only verb two problem types share in routing.md.
nodes.author: pbakaus

nodes.label: animate
nodes.what: Adds purposeful motion and state-change feedback.
nodes.when: Routed for `needs-motion`, only when the brief or direction asks for motion.
nodes.how: Additive last-tier verb; delight may call it.
nodes.author: pbakaus

nodes.label: delight
nodes.what: Adds personality and memorable touches to a correct but lifeless surface.
nodes.when: Routed for `personality`, only when the brief asks for character.
nodes.how: Additive last-tier verb that calls animate for motion; followed by polish.
nodes.author: pbakaus

nodes.label: extract
nodes.what: Pulls repeated UI into shared tokens and components.
nodes.when: Routed for `drift`: the same pattern copied 3+ times, raw values next to tokens, one-off components.
nodes.how: Structural tier, first in the chain; shared components change only behind a new prop that defaults to today's behaviour.
nodes.author: pbakaus

nodes.label: shape
nodes.what: Plans UX/UI for a feature before code is written.
nodes.when: Dispatched by /super-board lint for feature tickets with undefined UX; never typed as a refine-loop problem.
nodes.how: Requires init's PRODUCT.md; a redesign need found in the loop goes to openQuestions instead.
nodes.author: pbakaus

nodes.label: init
nodes.what: Captures durable product context in PRODUCT.md.
nodes.when: Suggested by /impeccable when PRODUCT.md is missing; not run by the refine loop.
nodes.how: Shape and document require it; its context feeds live mode.
nodes.author: pbakaus

nodes.label: document
nodes.what: Generates DESIGN.md from existing project code.
nodes.when: When DESIGN.md is missing; the refine loop reads DESIGN.md if present but never runs this.
nodes.how: Requires init; doctor feeds it when files go stale.
nodes.author: pbakaus

nodes.label: live
nodes.what: Visual variant mode: pick elements in the browser and generate alternatives.
nodes.when: Interactive iteration only; the refine loop forbids it as a problem type.
nodes.how: Fed by init's context and calls polish on the chosen variant.
nodes.author: pbakaus

nodes.label: overdrive
nodes.what: Pushes a design past conventional limits for a wow factor.
nodes.when: Interactive only; the refine loop never types a problem as overdrive.
nodes.how: A redesign-scale command, so the checker sends such needs to openQuestions.
nodes.author: pbakaus

nodes.label: super-board-preflight.sh
nodes.what: Builder pre-flight check: is a Ready card already done, already in progress, overlapping an open PR's files, or unclear?
nodes.when: Run once per batch of up to 5 Ready build cards by the wave's Pre-flight agent (or by the Builder as step 0 on the legacy backend), before any worktree.
nodes.how: Prints mechanical verdicts and near-miss candidates; the agent adds 'too big' and semantic matches, then returns proceed, hold, sequence or skipped. Hold and sequence move the card to Blocked with the block template; skipped leaves it in Ready.

nodes.label: super-board-pr-body.sh
nodes.what: Rewrites one marker block of a PR body (redcheck, status, problem, solution, ac, history, visual, risk) without clobbering other lanes' blocks.
nodes.when: Called by every lane when it updates its part of the PR, and with --skeleton by ui-refine-loop for a fresh body.
nodes.how: `--pr N --block <name> --expect-head <sha>` with --body-file or --append-file (history rows); `--time` prints local time in the config's timezone.

nodes.label: Blocked · 🙋 needs you
nodes.what: A card parked in Blocked with the 🙋 template and the `needs-you` label: a step only a human may take. There is no separate column.
nodes.when: The merge gate exits 7 (merge_policy: money, auth, destructive schema, over 400 lines) or 8 (a migration the robot may not run, or a declared human step).
nodes.how: The comment opens "🙋 Your turn on #N" with the exact commands as checkboxes; a human merges it, or comments `done` / labels `needs-you:done` so the planner's resume list sends it back to Review.

nodes.label: super-board-setup.py
nodes.what: The deterministic half of onboard: finds what is missing or old and fixes the must-haves, and handles boards and branches.
nodes.when: Run by onboard step 1 (check / fix), step 3 (board-rank, board-migrate, names) and step 4 (branch).
nodes.how: `fix` installs or refreshes skills, scripts, workflows, guard hooks and settings (via install.sh), removes super-refine / cleanup-wt / arch-loop folders, migrates config keys to v3, runs git init and adds Matt Pocock's skills, all backed up first. `board-migrate` adds missing columns and the three labels and moves Skipped cards to Done.

nodes.label: super-board-agents-md.py
nodes.what: The deterministic half of the AGENTS.md step: detect, backup, the managed super-board block, the CLAUDE.md pointer, coverage and size checks.
nodes.when: Run by onboard step 5 to stage the merge and at step 8 to write it; install.sh refreshes the managed block on re-install.
nodes.how: The agent merges rules semantically (duplicates once, conflicts asked one by one); the script proves every rule unit maps to a line (`coverage`), keeps AGENTS.md ≤ 200 lines with one marker pair, and writes atomically.

nodes.label: AGENTS.md + CLAUDE.md
nodes.what: The project's instruction files: AGENTS.md as the single source of truth with a managed super-board block, and CLAUDE.md as `@AGENTS.md` plus Claude-only rules.
nodes.when: Written at onboard step 8 when Eric chose to move his rules (or only add the section); the block is rewritten on re-install.
nodes.how: The block sits between `<!-- super-board:begin -->` and `<!-- super-board:end -->`, rendered from agents-md-block.md with a Writing table that links the writing standard; nothing outside the markers is touched.

nodes.label: super-board-settings.py
nodes.what: Merges hook blocks and permission allow rules into .claude/settings.json without losing anything.
nodes.when: Run by install.sh for the guard hooks, and by onboard step 6/8 for the permission lines and the protect-main hook.
nodes.how: `hooks <settings> <snippet>` and `allow <settings> <rules…>` keep every existing key, back the file up, write atomically, and leave an invalid settings.json untouched; `--dry-run` prints the diff onboard shows as "N lines".

nodes.label: super-board-env-check.sh
nodes.what: Says which env keys exist (present, empty or missing) without ever printing a value.
nodes.when: Run by onboard to detect SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN, POSTHOG_PERSONAL_API_KEY or migration DB URLs, and allowed in permissions for runs.
nodes.how: Reads .env.local or .env itself and prints one word per key; guard-secrets lets a plain call through while still blocking cat, grep or source on dotenv files.

nodes.label: custom source fetcher
nodes.what: The custom source: extra sources a project added in onboard (an http API, a CLI command, or an MCP server), stored in collect.custom[].
nodes.when: Run by onboard step 7 (classify, ping, add) and by /super-collect for every custom source (list, normalize).
nodes.how: `collect_custom.py` classifies the typed text, pings read-only before saving, refuses commands that look like they change something, and turns output into candidates with fp `custom|<name>|<key>`. MCP reads go through the agent and `normalize`.

nodes.label: get.sh
nodes.what: One-line installer: `curl -fsSL …/get.sh | bash` fetches the latest super-board release and runs install.sh.
nodes.when: Eric (or a user) runs it in a project folder to install or upgrade; options --target, --ref, --no-helper-skills, and --no-hooks / --protect-main passed through.
nodes.how: Downloads the release tarball, runs install.sh, adds Matt Pocock's skills via `npx skills@latest add mattpocock/skills` unless told not to, and prints the next step once.

nodes.label: plugin marketplace install
nodes.what: The Claude Code plugin form of the pack (marketplace.json + plugin.json): ships the seven skills only.
nodes.when: A user adds the marketplace and installs the plugin instead of running get.sh.
nodes.how: Skills carry the plugin prefix (/super-board:super-board onboard); onboard step 1 then installs the guard hooks, .claude/bin scripts and workflows a plugin cannot ship from the plugin's own copy.

nodes.label: onboard answers file
nodes.what: `.claude/super-board/onboard-answers.json`: every onboard answer, saved the moment it is given (gitignored).
nodes.when: Written after each answer; read when onboard re-runs or resumes after a halt.
nodes.how: Atomic writes; `last_step` drives the "Continue where you left off?" screen, and a finished setup's values fill the step-8 table on re-run.

nodes.label: upgrade record
nodes.what: `.claude/super-board/upgrade.json`: the version an install replaced, so onboard knows to upgrade a 2.x setup.
nodes.when: Written by install.sh (or get.sh) when it finds an older install.
nodes.how: super-board-setup.py fix reads it and reports "Upgraded for you": old folders removed, config keys migrated, labels mapped, Skipped cards moved to Done.

nodes.label: /git-sync
nodes.what: Commits the working tree as one commit per logical change, merge-pulls, pushes the current branch without force, and reports what it did.
nodes.when: Eric runs /git-sync or says "sync", "commit and push" or "pull and push", usually at the end of a piece of work.
nodes.how: Stages each group by path (never `git add -A`), refuses secrets, writes the host's commit format or the writing standard, gates `supabase/` changes on a migration file and advisors, then `git pull --no-rebase` and `git push`. The default or a protected branch needs a yes.
nodes.author: EricTechPro

edges.when: card enters at Review; always on the session model

edges.label: moves card to QA
edges.when: draft PR opened and comments posted

edges.label: writes gaps red-first
edges.when: the test-gap check finds a High gap

edges.when: the repo has tdd-v2 (used instead of plain tdd)

edges.label: diagnoses failures

edges.label: proves the pass
edges.when: before a pass handoff

edges.when: the right flow is unclear

edges.label: judges coverage
edges.when: deciding what is worth testing per component type

edges.label: writes unit tests
edges.when: the ladder stops at unit or integration in TS/JS

edges.label: writes e2e specs
edges.when: the browser is the thing that broke, or standalone crawl specs

edges.label: moves card

views.title: super-board pack
views.caption: Collect verified tickets into the board; the board contains Build → QA → Review. UI refinement, visuals and Git sync are standalone skills. Open a family or step for its tools and policies.

views.title: /super-board · five verbs
views.caption: Onboard sets up; lint makes cards ready; run delegates the lanes. Status inspects a run; stop halts it.

views.title: /super-board lint · Phase 4 routing
views.caption: Interactive-only skills live here, never inside an unattended worker. Ticket-format fixes (criteria 16–18) and catch-alls get an inline draft.

views.title: /super-board run · main steps
views.caption: One wave: classify → pre-flight → delegate → merge → done. Up to min(16, CPUs − 2) cards run at once; the runtime queues the rest. Pre-flight checks batches of 5. Open a step for scripts and policies.

nodes.label: Classify cards
nodes.what: Route qa, bug and feature cards by label. Classify unlabelled cards as bug or feature.
nodes.when: Each Ready card enters the classifier. Existing type labels take priority.
nodes.how: Read the issue body and comments. Judge complexity as low, medium or high; choose the worker model tier.

nodes.label: Pre-flight check
nodes.what: Check whether a Ready build card is already done or in progress. Flag overlap, unclear scope and excessive size.
nodes.when: Before any worktree or Builder starts. Check build cards in batches of up to five.
nodes.how: Combine mechanical checks with semantic matches. Return proceed, hold, sequence or skipped.

nodes.label: Delegate to lanes
nodes.what: Run the Build, QA and Review lane agents. QA-labelled cards skip Building.
nodes.when: After pre-flight allows a build card to proceed. QA and Review cards enter their current lane.
nodes.how: Build advances to QA, then Review. A non-advanced exit stops that card’s chain; Review uses the session model. The runtime caps concurrent agents at min(16, CPUs − 2), and queues the rest.

nodes.label: Merge gate
nodes.what: Re-prove the branch under an atomic merge lock. Apply merge policy before squash-merging.
nodes.when: Once Review passes. Human-only steps park the card in Blocked.
nodes.how: Check the current base and permitted migrations. Match the PR head before merge; clean the worktree afterwards.

nodes.label: Done
nodes.what: Squash-merge the approved PR and clean its worktree. Reconcile the returned card result.
nodes.when: After Review and the merge gate pass. Report the wave before selecting the next one.
nodes.how: Record merged, bounced, blocked or failed outcomes. Repeat waves until the board drains or a halt gate fires.

views.title: super-build · skills by ticket type
views.caption: An explicit `Skills:` line wins; otherwise the type label picks the chain. Each PR stays under 400 changed lines. grilling is forbidden here and lives in lint.

views.title: super-qa · test plan, gap check, evidence
views.caption: Issue-scoped inside a run (qa-labelled cards skip Building); standalone it crawls routes and files onto the Super Ultimate QA board.

views.title: super-review · own pass, memory, merge gate
views.caption: Fresh review, adversarial grounding and refactor findings. Passing review enters the merge gate; human-only steps open their own view.

views.title: /super-collect · fetch, verify, file
views.caption: Fetch → fresh verifier → confirm → Backlog. Five built-in sources plus custom ones; collection never moves a card to Ready.

nodes.label: Fetch enabled sources
nodes.what: Fetch the enabled built-in sources. Include any custom sources added in onboard.
nodes.when: When /super-collect runs for the project. Use the requested window or the default 14 days.
nodes.how: Read the selected adapters and findings. Send each candidate to a fresh verifier.

nodes.label: Verify each candidate
nodes.what: Check whether each candidate is real and still happening. Reject fixed or duplicate problems.
nodes.when: After source adapters return candidates. Use one fresh verifier for each candidate.
nodes.how: Verify against the project evidence. Mark unclear candidates needs-triage before filing.

nodes.label: Confirm the plan
nodes.what: Show the proposed filing plan. Keep collection dry-run by default.
nodes.when: After verification produces the candidate results. Before writing tickets to the board.
nodes.how: Present the plan table for confirmation. Use --yes when filing is already authorized.

nodes.label: File verified tickets
nodes.what: File verified problems into Backlog. Apply fingerprints and duplicate checks.
nodes.when: After confirmation or an authorized --yes run. File candidates marked file or needs-triage.
nodes.how: Use one filing entry point for all sources. Route bugs, features and fixes separately from refactors.

views.title: /ui-refine-loop · main steps
views.caption: Standalone: direction → check → fix → review → draft PR. Default 5 rounds; stop after two clean P0/P1 checks, two reverted rounds or a dead agent.

nodes.label: Grill + save direction
nodes.what: Read the target code and clarify the intended UI. Save taste and direction for the loop.
nodes.when: At the start of a standalone refine task. Before unattended checking and fixing begins.
nodes.how: Ask at most ten questions. Write the agreed direction into the taste file.

nodes.label: Check the UI
nodes.what: Use fresh checkers to identify UI problems. Rank typed findings before a fix.
nodes.when: At the start of each refinement round. Check the chosen page or component.
nodes.how: Capture screenshots and run critique or audit. Route typed findings to the appropriate fix verbs.

nodes.label: Fix by routed verbs
nodes.what: Apply the Impeccable verbs matched to the findings. Run polish last.
nodes.when: After checkers have ranked the problems. Use a fresh fixer for the round.
nodes.how: Chain the verbs in their prescribed order. Keep additive motion within the brief’s permission.

nodes.label: Review each fix
nodes.what: Grade every fix with a finish reviewer. Record or revert each round.
nodes.when: After the round’s fixer completes. Run five rounds by default unless a stop condition fires.
nodes.how: Write the outcome to the refine ledger. Stop after two clean checks, two reverted rounds or a dead agent.

nodes.label: Draft the PR
nodes.what: Create the final draft PR. Include a Before | After evidence table.
nodes.when: When the standalone refinement loop finishes. After fixes have received their finish review.
nodes.how: Use the PR body marker blocks. Follow the writing standard with humanizer.

views.title: impeccable fix verbs · routing

notes: Refreshed to super-board v3.0.0 (feat/sb-cleanup @ b67241e1, 28 commits after cd199b2d). Source paths are repo-root-relative.

Board: seven columns, no Skipped (a dropped card is closed as not planned → Done with 🤷). Labels qa · bug · feature route cards; qa skips Building; the classifier adds feature or bug, never qa. The per-board `variant` is gone and a `qa-only` config is refused with exit 65 until onboard upgrades it.

Onboarding is an 8-step wizard (Checks · GitHub · Board · Branch · AGENTS.md · Policies · Bug sources · Review) backed by super-board-setup.py (check, fix, migrate-config, names, branch, board-rank, board-migrate). New view sb-onboard; its steps are edge labels, not nodes.

Merge policy and DB migrations live in the merge gate (super-board-merge-policy.py): money, auth, destructive schema or a diff over auto_max_lines (400 changed lines, lockfiles/generated/snapshots/migration SQL excluded) exits 7; a migration outside allowed_envs, a failed migrate or a declared human step exits 8. Both park the card in Blocked with the 🙋 checklist and the needs-you label, with no extra column; `done` sends it back through the planner's resume list.

Builder pre-flight (super-board-preflight.sh, a Pre-flight phase in super-board-wave.js, batches of 5) checks already done / in progress / file overlap / unclear / too big before any card is built. Lint has 18 criteria now: 15 = too big (split via /to-tickets), 16–18 = ticket format.

Writing standard (references/writing-standard.md): commits `<emoji> [type] scope: subject` + bullets, tickets Problem · Context · Fix · AC · Risk · Blocked by, PR bodies in marker blocks rewritten per lane with super-board-pr-body.sh, comments `[role] [label] status`, prose through humanizer when installed. That is why every lane view now shows pr-body and humanizer.
super-collect gained custom sources (collect_custom.py: http, cli, mcp) added in onboard's "➕ Add another source", with fingerprint `custom|<name>|<key>` and the same verifier and filer.

Install: get.sh one-liner, a plugin marketplace (skills only; onboard adds hooks, scripts and workflows), install.sh with grouped output and an upgrade record, and super-board-settings.py for hook and allow-line merges. There is a new install view under root. env-check (key names only) is allowed through guard-secrets. The AGENTS.md helper is super-board-agents-md.py.

Added nodes: preflight, pr-body, needs-you, setup-py, agents-md-py, agents-file, settings-py, env-check, collect-custom, get-sh, plugin-mkt, onboard-answers, upgrade-json. Added views: sb-onboard, install. Removed edges: sb-onb-push (now settings-push in sb-onboard), h-install and h-ships (now install-sh → settings-py and install-sh → hooks). Nothing was renamed.

Also since 88c27812: super-review truth-check sub-agents get a fixed verbatim brief (Over-engineering never blocks), and status lists columns in board order with Backlog. Disagreement: the coordinator listed 'labels qa/bug/feature routing'. That matches, with one addition: no label is also built (treated as feature).

Kept as-is but stale in the files: the merge protocol and the wave.js `humanApprovesMerge` arg still mention human_approves_merge, which onboard now migrates into merge_policy. super-qa standalone still files onto the separate Super Ultimate QA board.
The Builder only proposes a /to-tickets split in a PR comment when a build outgrows the cap; it does not run to-tickets, so there is no super-build → to-tickets edge. lint does dispatch it.

Unchanged from v2: ui-refine-loop is standalone, now stated in super-review and super-qa as 'file a UI ticket; a human can run /ui-refine-loop'. cleanup-wt still runs at SessionStart and post-merge. qa-test-planner, testing-strategy, vitest and playwright-best-practices are still not installed in EricOS.
